forces.title: Moderating 5G investment cycle post-peak rollout
forces.description: Following extensive nationwide 5G network rollouts from FY23-FY25, the telecom sector is transitioning from large-scale coverage expansion to selective capacity augmentation and fibre densification. This leads to a moderation in operator capital expenditure intensity, decreasing from an estimated 22% in FY26 to 19% in FY27. For Telecom Equipment & Infrastructure providers, this signifies a shift from a high-growth 'peak build' phase to a more moderate 'optimize and densify' phase, impacting order books and revenue growth rates.
forces.source_title: Telecom Revenue to Grow 12-14% in FY27 as ARPU Rises 10%

forces.title: Global electronics supply chain realignment drives India's EMS opportunity
forces.description: Geopolitical risks, the pursuit of supply chain resilience (China+1 strategy), and regulatory pressures (like PLI schemes) are structurally transforming global electronics manufacturing. This shift leads OEMs to diversify production networks, benefiting emerging hubs like India. For Telecom Network Equipment manufacturers, this realignment offers a significant opportunity to scale domestic production and integration into global value chains, moving beyond cost-based competition to strategic partnership.

forces.title: Robust government policy support and investments for telecom infrastructure
forces.description: The Indian government continues to prioritize telecom infrastructure expansion, evident from significant budget allocations (Rs. 73,990 crore in FY27 to DoT) and major programs like BharatNet (USD 17.0 billion deployment) and the PLI scheme for telecom and networking products (Rs. 1,950 crore). These initiatives aim to boost rural connectivity, facilitate 5G deployment, and promote indigenous manufacturing, creating substantial demand and a supportive ecosystem for Telecom Equipment & Infrastructure providers.

forces.title: Rapid 5G network expansion and subscriber migration
forces.description: India has seen a rapid rollout of 5G services, with 5.23 lakh 5G Base Transceiver Stations (BTSs) installed across 99.9% of districts by February 2026. 5G subscriptions reached 430 million by end-2025, accounting for 35% of total mobile subscriptions, and are projected to continue growing as 4G users migrate. This widespread deployment and ongoing subscriber adoption sustain high demand for 5G-related Telecom Network Equipment and upgrades to passive infrastructure.

forces.title: Absence of deep domestic component supply chain for electronics manufacturing
forces.description: India's EMS industry, while growing rapidly, faces a structural vulnerability in its shallow domestic component supply chain. Unlike established manufacturing hubs, India remains heavily reliant on imported components for semiconductors, displays, PCBs, and other critical parts, even for domestically assembled products. This dependence limits local value capture and exposes Telecom Network Equipment manufacturers to forex risks, import duties, and supply volatility, hindering the sector's move up the value curve.

forces.title: Increased focus on rural telecom infrastructure and connectivity programs
forces.description: Government initiatives, such as the BharatNet program and the Amended BharatNet Programme, are channeling significant financial support (e.g., Rs. 2,432 crore for Andhra Pradesh) towards strengthening rural telecom infrastructure. These efforts aim to enhance last-mile connectivity, upgrade network resilience, and expand broadband access across thousands of Gram Panchayats. This sustained focus creates predictable and substantial demand for Telecom Network Equipment and Towers & Passive Infrastructure in underserved rural areas.

forces.title: Growing demand for fibre densification to support 5G and broadband
forces.description: As 5G networks mature and broadband penetration increases, there is an ongoing need for fibre densification to support higher data consumption and improved network quality. CareEdge Ratings notes that operators are transitioning from large-scale 5G coverage expansion to selective capacity augmentation and fibre densification. This sustained investment in optical transport and fibre infrastructure represents a continuous demand driver for Telecom Network Equipment manufacturers, ensuring ongoing upgrade and expansion projects beyond initial 5G rollout.
forces.source_title: Telecom Revenue to Grow 12-14% in FY27 as ARPU Rises 10%

forces.title: Indigenous equipment procurement driving domestic vendor orders
forces.description: Bengaluru-based gear maker Tejas Networks securing a three-year deal (2024-2027) from Vodafone Idea to supply backhaul equipment for its 4G and 5G networks exemplifies a growing trend towards indigenous procurement. This specific order highlights telecom operators' reliance on domestic manufacturers for critical network components, potentially driven by policy support for 'Made in India' initiatives. Such deals provide a significant tailwind for Indian Telecom Network Equipment companies, reinforcing local expertise and manufacturing capabilities.

viewpoints.title: Telecom operators exit peak 5G investment cycle, moderating capex intensity
viewpoints.description: CareEdge Ratings observes that India's telecom sector is moving beyond its peak 5G investment cycle, with nationwide rollouts largely complete. This moderation in operator capex intensity, projected to decline from 22% in FY26 to 19% in FY27, is expected to structurally improve operators' financial profiles by boosting free cash flow and accelerating deleveraging. For Telecom Equipment & Infrastructure providers, this implies a potential deceleration in new orders compared to the aggressive build-out phase, shifting focus towards maintenance, upgrades, and capacity augmentation rather than large-scale coverage expansion.
viewpoints.source_title: Telecom Revenue to Grow 12-14% in FY27 as ARPU Rises 10%

viewpoints.title: India's EMS market poised for significant growth, including telecom infrastructure
viewpoints.description: KPMG highlights India's Electronic Manufacturing Services (EMS) market is set to experience rapid growth, projected to exceed USD 150 billion by FY30 at over 25% CAGR. This expansion is driven by global supply chain realignments, robust policy incentives, and surging domestic demand. While currently concentrated in mobile and consumer electronics, diversification into higher-complexity segments like telecom infrastructure is underway, presenting a significant opportunity for hardware manufacturers within the Telecom Network Equipment node.

viewpoints.title: Strong government support and investments to boost telecom infrastructure growth
viewpoints.description: IBEF reports significant government allocation and investment in India's telecommunications sector, reinforcing infrastructure expansion. The Union Budget 2026–27 allocated Rs. 73,990 crore (US$ 8.37 billion) to the Department of Telecommunications, alongside a USD 17.0 billion commitment for the BharatNet programme and Rs. 1,950 crore for the PLI scheme for telecom and networking products. These initiatives signal a robust policy environment and sustained investment in rural connectivity, 5G deployment, and indigenous manufacturing, providing strong tailwinds for Telecom Equipment & Infrastructure providers.

demand_drivers.description: Proliferation of smartphones, laptops, and IoT-enabled industrial systems drives demand for electronics manufacturing capacity.
Increasing electrification of industries like automotive, energy, and manufacturing expands demand for electronic components and systems.
OEMs increasingly outsource manufacturing to EMS providers for flexibility and reduced capital investment as products become more complex and production cycles accelerate.
Growth in telecommunications infrastructure, including 5G rollout and fibre densification, drives demand for associated equipment.

market_sizing.methodology: Global EMS market estimate at approximately USD 640-650 billion in 2025, with projections for continued expansion.

demand_drivers.description: Growing internal consumption of electronic products drives demand for local manufacturing.
Increased integration into global value chains and export opportunities boost manufacturing output.
Global OEMs' increasing reliance on EMS providers for manufacturing.
Government schemes like PLI for electronics and IT hardware stimulate investment and production.
Shift from China-centric supply chains towards multi-node networks benefits India's manufacturing.

new_opportunities.description: While currently concentrated in mobile and consumer electronics, there's a nascent opportunity to expand into higher-complexity segments like automotive, industrial, and telecom infrastructure, offering higher margins and longer product lifecycles.

market_sizing.methodology: India's EMS market has expanded from USD 10-12 billion in FY20 to USD 40-45 billion in FY25, driven by domestic demand, export growth and outsourcing trends.

demand_drivers.description: The PLI scheme incentivizes domestic manufacturing and R&D for telecom and networking products.
Aims to strengthen India's role in global telecom technology development.
Supports startups, MSMEs, academia, and industry players in developing advanced telecom solutions.

market_sizing.methodology: Allocation for the Production-Linked Incentive (PLI) scheme for telecom and networking products in the Union Budget 2026–27.

Strengthening the foundation for 5G services and future 6G.

demand_drivers.description: Investment by towercos to support telecom operators in extending network reach to rural areas.
